about: #452 (spec #450, owner decisions on #446) — the letterhead reading's regression set: every row is a real model call through #451's step (prompts/letterhead-reader.md + the source-quote guard in letterheadReader.ts), and EVERY row must be right on name and city. Run it deliberately (pnpm --filter @jobcrush/api eval:letterhead), never in fast-lane CI; re-run it before believing any change to the reading instructions. Rows 1-72 are the 'never worse than main' table from branch t/409-letterhead (3b93bdd) with each 'lost on main' row moved to the right answer; the rest are the shapes found since (#409 round 4, #444, letter-spacing, no city, postal addresses). Invented values only: the repo is public — and never the canonical placeholder 'Jane Doe': measured 2026-10-28 on the CLI route, the model reads that name as sample text and answers null about one time in three on the same shapes another invented name passes every time, so the source table's Jane Doe rows carry 'Elena Marsh' here, shapes unchanged. The same goes for a real celebrity's stage name (the table's MADONNA rows, one word + 'Singer', nulled one run in three): they carry the invented 'ZOLARA'.

convention.name: The person's own name as the CV writes it: order, capitals, credentials kept ('John Smith, PMP', 'Smith, John'). A name split over lines is one name; letters printed one by one are joined ('E L E N A  M A R S H' -> 'JANE DOE'), the only repair allowed. Null when the letterhead has no name.
convention.location: A place the letterhead gives as where the person is, as the CV writes it: a standalone place line ('London', 'Greater London', 'Singapore 018956', 'La Chaux-de-Fonds 2300'), or the city part of a postal address — the line holding postcode/city and what sits beside it on that line ('1000 Lausanne', 'London SW1A 1AA', '1000 Lausanne, Switzerland'), never the street line. When the letterhead gives both a postal address and a separate place line, the separate place line is the answer (the address is where mail goes; the line is where the person says they are). A job's place, a line from a job or a bullet, an employer's address, 'Remote', a link, or a place word inside a name never count. Null when the letterhead gives no such place.
convention.input: Each row's letterhead is followed by a short Experience block (the eval appends it), as the source table did, so the model always sees a CV and not a bare header; the step's own 2000-char cut applies.
